To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Achilles tension increases the risk of injury, (2) the primary fracture mode is calcaneal fracture, (3) fracture initiation coincides with peak tibial force, (4) fracture risk can be estimated using a Weibul regression model, and (5) fracture risk can also be estimated using a closed form survivor function
the Achilles tension increases the incidence of calcaneal fractures and that a closed form model was developed to predict fracture risk to the foot/ ankle complex in terms of peak tibial force.

the axial injury tolerance of isolated foot/ankle specimens is 3.7 to 8.4 kN, depending on the age and gender of the test subject and whether or not there was experimentally simulated Achilles tendon tension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the axial injury tolerance of human lower extremity and the effect of muscle tension on fracture mode.
the effect of active muscle tension on the axial tolerance of the foot and ankle complex.
the axial injury tolerance of foot/ankles and the effects of Achilles tension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Achilles tension does not change the mode of fracture in the foot/ankles complex but rather the location where fracture initiates.
the addition of Achilles tendon tension increases axial injury tolerance of isolated lower extremity cadaveric specimens.
the addition of Achilles muscle tension during pre-impact bracing significantly increases the risk of fracture of the foot and ankle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Achilles tendon is an important contributor to the injury tolerance of the foot.
axial injury tolerance of human foot/ankles is dependent upon peak tibial force, age, gender, and body mass.
the Achilles tension is an important variable in axial loading injury to the foot/ ankle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Achilles tension increases the risk of foot and ankle fracture during blunt axial loading of the foot, and that the risk of foot fracture can be estimated using a closed form survivor function.
the Achilles tendon plays a critical role in determining the injury tolerance of the foot and ankle complex.
the Achilles tendon is an important internal load path in the lower leg that must be considered in the design of crashworthy vehicle structures.
